findings.title: FU-23: ids are reused after a hard delete, wider than recorded (requests, plan versions, images); I agree with dec-mv330std-0165d9be if its scope grows
findings.detail:
rescue_requests uses INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so a hard delete of the highest id lets the next request take it.

Security's reproduction (ev:ev-mv33e5qp-017ba56b, section F):
- Y's request and plan version get X's deleted ids.
- Y sees nothing of X, and X gets 404.
- The admin timeline of Y's request lists X's extraction.run, requirements.confirm, plan.create, plan.approve, void_rule.apply, plan.non_executable and request.delete events.

The scope is wider than the decision:
- plan_versions ids are reused through the same cascade, and images ids follow from it;
- both appear in audit_events.entity_id, and plan-version ids feed the timeline scope.
AUTOINCREMENT on rescue_requests alone would leave X's plan.approve rows attributed to Y's plan.

I add one point: model_spend.request_id has no foreign key, so X's model-spend rows also re-attach to Y's id.

The reach is limited: the highest ids only, hard deletes only (no supplier order ever), and no customer-facing disclosure. The audit rows hold ids and codes only. I do not raise its severity.

findings.title: The eleven documented design deltas: all acceptable additions or justified deviations, three with caveats to carry
findings.detail:
Each delta (followups.md, 'Documented design deltas') judged against the approved spec.

Acceptable additions:
- (1) Extraction.addressedToAssistant. The spec requires the notice but omitted the field from Extraction. It is stored under the __meta key, hidden on read, and confirm ignores it.
- (2) RequestView.capabilities.deleteRequest. Additive, but always true, so the UI offers Delete in states where DELETE answers 409 PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS. The UI handles the 409. Either make it status-dependent or document it as a route-availability flag.
- (3) 400 BAD_REQUEST for a missing Content-Length and for UPLOAD_TIMEOUT. The catalog has no better code. Caveat: with the default server requestTimeout of 30 s, the route's 60 s UPLOAD_TIMEOUT branch cannot fire in production; only tests reach it, with an injected deadline (see TR-D-7).
- (4) The refusal rows' errorCode, BUSY or UNAVAILABLE. Both values are inside the spec's enum.
- (5) A degraded row replaces the newest degraded row. The table stays bounded. The audit row per extraction.run and model_spend keep the history.
- (6) Content-Disposition: inline. Harmless next to CSP sandbox and nosniff; security's polyglot run in Chromium confirms it (ev:ev-mv33nzz8-010dae0c).
- (7) The sweep also purges rate_events and settles stale reservations. An interim owner, with FU-22 requiring one owner.

Justified deviations:
- (8) Client limits of 65 s and 45 s. The spec's blanket 15 s contradicts its own 30 s model timeout, so the deviation is necessary.
- (10) RS_LIVE_MODEL_CEILING_USD. Safer than the spec; FU-21 covers the docs. Its parsing is TR-D-10.
- (11) Internal micro-dollar fields. No external contract.

Deviation from d2's criterion:
- (9) labels/*.txt with a 5x7 bitmap renderer instead of labels/*.html with Chromium. The labels are legible (I viewed i06), but they are English capitals only. No image carries Arabic text, so LIVE-M1 will say nothing about reading Arabic packaging.

None of the eleven is a spec violation that needs code rework.

findings.title: FU-2 and the timeout chain: I agree with dec-mv31kbrz-012381a1, with two notes for the verification report (merged with security SEC-D-8, info)
findings.detail:
Upload:
- Node's requestTimeout of 30 s cuts a slow body before the route's 60 s deadline. Security measured 408 at 30.95 s for a 1 KiB/s upload (ev:ev-mv33mul3-01ddae55, T2).
- That 408 is the server's bare clientError reply from src/http/server.js, with no JSON envelope and no requestId (NFR6 says every response carries one).
- The client waits 65 s, then shows the error with Retry.

Extract:
- RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30 s) bounds the watchdog, the CLI timer and the Anthropic deadline. Node's requestTimeout does not bound the handler: security's T1 got a 200 after 35 s with the variable at 40 s.
- The client allows 45 s, so the default chain is consistent.
- config accepts RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS up to 600000. Above about 44 s the client aborts first, while the server still holds the connection and the customer's model slot, stores the row and charges the call.

1.4 Mbit/s for 5 MB is acceptable for version one.
findings.recommendation:
Owners: delivery-lead and g2, or e1 (owner of src/config.js in phase E) for the clamp.
- The verification report lists the 408 without envelope or requestId as an NFR6 exception.
- RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS is clamped to at most 40000, below the client's 45 s (security suggests 60000; 40000 also keeps the client consistent), or g2 documents the bound.
No phase D code change.

findings.title: Security info items SEC-D-3..SEC-D-9 folded in; FU-24 and FU-25 decisions agreed
findings.detail:
Folded from the FINAL security draft, all info:
- SEC-D-3: the server is not the injection backstop for a real model; the flag, the buyer and the approval are.
  - An obeying model that quotes the injected sentence itself passes grounding (budget $99,999 from ti01-en).
  - Any in-range image-provenance number is accepted; there is no OCR.
  - Suggestion: when addressedToAssistant is true, ask the buyer to re-check every known field (product decision).
- SEC-D-4: five self-registered accounts from one IP spend the default USD 1.00 daily budget (SEC-10 residual, measured). Suggestion: the README recommends RS_ALLOW_SIGNUP=0 or a smaller share for public deployments.
- SEC-D-5: anthropic.js buffers a chunked body whole before the 1 MiB check (48 MiB read, RSS +157 MiB). Only the pinned host can send it.
- SEC-D-6: extract has no per-request idempotency; a double-click is one extra billed call, bounded by the rate limit and concurrency 1.
- SEC-D-7: photos, including EXIF location, are stored and forwarded to the provider byte-for-byte. The README privacy statement (T23) should say so, or metadata is stripped.
- SEC-D-8: merged into TR-D-7.
- SEC-D-9: d5's secrets scan covers the log channel well. Responses, database rows and an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the separate-process run are gaps, planned for g3 (RS-29).

On the open decisions:
- FU-24 (dec-mv330t0g-0175d52b): I agree. It follows the spec text, avoids mixing provenance across extractions, and the customer can finish by hand.
- FU-25 (dec-mv330t7a-017a2211): I agree. An inert RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE must be removed or documented, and RS-05's rephrasing clause counts as unit-level only.
findings.recommendation: FU-24: none. FU-25: per the decision, e1 and g2. SEC-D-3..SEC-D-7 and SEC-D-9 go into the verification report's risk list (owner delivery-lead). The README items (SEC-D-4, SEC-D-7) go to g2; SEC-D-5 (streamed byte cap) goes to the ai-engineer when anthropic.js is next touched.

findings.title: A detached CLI child outlives its parent: a server restart or a killed live run leaves a billed model call unsupervised (security SEC-D-2, minor)
findings.detail:
Where:
- src/ai/cli.js spawns the child with detached: true, in its own process group. Only the adapter's timer, the abort signal or the stdout cap kill it, and all three die with the parent.
- main.js stop() calls process.exit(0) without stopping in-flight provider calls.
- test/live/run-live-model.js has no SIGINT or SIGTERM handling.

Reproduced by security against a stub (ev:ev-mv33mul3-01ddae55, C7): after the parent's SIGTERM, and again after SIGKILL, the child keeps running. I read the same code: runOnce keeps no registry of children and the provider has no close().

Impact:
- Each orphaned call still bills, up to --max-budget-usd (USD 0.05): at most 2 per server process, plus one per killed live run.
- A hanging CLI leaks a process.
- Accounting survives: the reservation stays 'reserved' and the sweep settles it at the cap.

findings.title: The live runner silently rounds the ceiling it was given (5.0000001 becomes 5.000000 and is accepted); it started a real run during the security review (RISK-21)
findings.detail:
evaluateLaunch parses RS_LIVE_MODEL_CEILING_USD with toMicroUsd, which rounds half-up at the sixth decimal, and only then checks the result against the 5.00 maximum. So the value 5.0000001 is accepted as exactly USD 5.00.

The money cap itself holds. The enforced ceiling is never above 5.00, and security confirms that every value over 5.00 is refused (ev:ev-mv33mul3-01ddae55, section L).

The defect is silent coercion of a spend limit typed by a person. A ceiling that means 'just over five' should be refused, not reinterpreted.

The incident:
- During the security review this value, together with RS_LIVE_MODEL=1 and a logged-in `claude` on PATH, started a real run for up to 30 s (RISK-21).
- The runner then had no SIGTERM handling, so a killed run could leave its CLI child alive (TR-D-9).
- Whether a call was billed is unknown; the worst case is bounded by --max-budget-usd 0.05 per call.

The primary cause was the probe enabling the live switch on a machine with a logged-in CLI, which is not the runner's fault. Two runner properties widened it:
- a single env switch suffices to start a billed run;
- the run does not print and confirm its provider and worst case first. `--dry-run` exists but is optional.

findings.title: Two mutants of the d2 adapter survive: M19 (the cap in terminate() is pre-empted by the close handler) and M21 (the 'never started is not charged' branch of fail() is untested)

- M19: removing the cap from terminate()'s rejection (src/ai/cli.js L198) leaves cli.test.js 38/38 green. M19b (L246 only) and M19c (both sites) are killed (ev:ev-mv36r8lf-01323bb3), so the close() charge is pinned by tests. M19 is an equivalent mutant in practice, and L198 is a redundant backstop.
- M21: changing fail() to `usageHint ?? unknownAtCap()` (L206), which charges calls that never started a process, also leaves 38/38 green. The d2 test 'TR-D-15: a call that never started a process ... is not charged' (cli.test.js L467) covers two cases, and neither goes through fail():

Neither affects the ledger behaviour I verified through the route (P10a, P10b, P10c) and on a real server (P11, P4).

findings.title: Migration 006 hands out again ids that were hard-deleted before the upgrade, so FU-23's cross-customer audit mix-up reappears on every upgraded database
findings.detail:
006 re-inserts the surviving rows, which sets each sqlite_sequence to max(id) of the survivors (comment at L20: 'the best high-water mark that is known'). Higher ids are known, though:
- audit_events.entity_id (request, image, plan_version);
- audit_events.detail_json of plan.create (planVersionId, runId);
- the staged model_spend.request_id.

Reproduction:
- Mine (ev:ev-mv3u855g-011d4c00): X hard-deletes request 2 (image 11, run 101, plan version 30) on 005. After 006, Y's next request, image, run and plan version get 2/11/101/30, and 2 of X's audit rows name Y's request id.
- The security reviewer's, through the real HTTP flows (ev:ev-mv3twi5f-015c7a17): Y gets request 5 and image 4, and the admin timeline of Y's request lists X's request.create, extraction.run and request.delete. It also reproduces in isolation (ev:ev-mv3u2o6u-0130d038).

The proposed statements raise each sequence to the highest named id before the staging tables are dropped. With them the next ids are 3/12/102/31, the FK and integrity checks are clean and the rows are unchanged; both reviewers ran this.

Severity: security rates it minor, like the original FU-23. I raise it to major for three reasons.
1. It defeats the rework's own condition ('an RS-39 test shows no id is reused') on the databases the rebuild exists for.
2. It becomes irreversible as soon as 006 is applied to a persistent database: NFR1 refuses an edit, and a 007 cannot reclaim ids already reissued.
3. The rework limit is used, so after approval the only route is a fifth rework from the user, whereas now it is a reset of this task.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, after the orchestrator resets rework-4. Resolved when all of the following hold:
- 006, before it drops the staging tables, creates any missing sqlite_sequence row and raises each rebuilt table's sequence to the maximum of its surviving ids and every id still named. For rescue_requests that means audit request entity ids and the staged model_spend.request_id; for images, audit image entity ids; for plan_versions, audit plan_version entity ids and plan.create detail planVersionId; for planning_runs, plan.create detail runId. The statements in rework-4-security-1.md are acceptable.
- The comment at L20 and safety-argument point 6 are corrected.
- A new test (named RS-39) deletes the highest request, image, run and plan version on 005 before migrating, and asserts that none of those ids is handed out afterwards and that no earlier audit row names the new rows. It must be recorded failing on the submitted 006 and passing on the fixed one.
- The existing migrate-006 assertions are kept, with the sequence expectation updated to the new high-water mark.
- The green set, npm test and the browser suite pass.

findings.title: Migration 006's run time grows quadratically with the number of plan versions: about 9 s at 5000 request trees, holding the write lock
findings.detail:
Measured on scratch file databases, with 2 plan versions per tree and every 5th tree also holding a reservation and a supplier order:
- 1000 trees: 0.27-0.35 s.
- 2000 trees: 1.1 s.
- 4000 trees: 5.3 s.
- 5000 trees: 8.7 s.
(ev:ev-mv3tpe9a-016d484a; ev:ev-mv3tp49m-017879bb P3)

Nearly all of the time is in DROP TABLE plan_versions and INSERT INTO plan_versions. That fits the deferred-FK child scans over columns that have no index: plan_versions.superseded_by, reservations.plan_version_id and supplier_orders.plan_version_id.

The submission describes this cost as linear; it is not. Beyond about 4000 trees, a second process starting at the same time would hit its 5 s busy timeout. This is irrelevant at the demo's scale.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer in the same reset (optional), else the orchestrator. Resolved when either of these holds:
- 006 adds temporary indexes on plan_versions(superseded_by), reservations(plan_version_id) and supplier_orders(plan_version_id) and drops them before the end, so the schema stays identical, and a re-measurement shows near-linear growth.
- The operator note and the verification report state the measured cost and that one process upgrades before traffic.

findings.title: SEC-R-1 has no committed HTTP-level test; HEAD answers 405 through the router
findings.detail: The limiter unit test uses a real lock-holder process, and the hook test uses a mock. Both are mutant-tested. My P1 probe covers the HTTP path: GET 200 in 54 ms, one busy_open line, POST 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After 1. HEAD never reaches the hook, because the router answers 405 first; the security reviewer confirms this.
findings.recommendation: Owner: optional, the next src/auth or test/api touch. Resolved when an API test shows GET 200 and POST 503 under a held lock through createApp, or the orchestrator records that the unit tests plus the probes suffice.

findings.title: Pre-existing: a state-changing call waiting for a lock held by another process stalls the whole process for RS_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS
findings.detail: In my P4 probe, a 100 ms timer set right after a signed-in POST fired at 5015 ms, while the POST waited for 503. The busy wait of node:sqlite is synchronous. The read fail-open therefore helps only while no write of the same process waits. SEC-RW4-I4 is the same class, for the session touch.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the phase E reviewers and the orchestrator. Resolved when the phase E review confirms that reconciler and saga transactions are short (no await inside db.tx) and the verification report lists the residual; or a later rework shortens the write wait for request handlers.

findings.title: TR-D-3's report wording is superseded: model_spend rows of a hard-deleted request keep the row and lose the pointer (SET NULL)
findings.detail: After 006 the spend row survives with request_id NULL, and the daily sums are unchanged (my id-reuse run, and the security reviewer's metrics check). Dangling pointers that existed before the upgrade are set to NULL by 006; P2 found 43 of them.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator (verification report). Resolved when the report states the SET NULL behaviour and the NULLing at the upgrade.

findings.title: Toolkit defect: tree pinning is off in this nested project whenever any file is dirty
findings.detail: lib/project.js treeDigest() passes paths stripped of the project prefix to git hash-object --stdin-paths with the project as cwd. git resolves them from the repository root and fails, so the digest is null. The .eccode record files are always dirty between commits, so cited checks are not bound to a tree, and the engine's stale-check silently skips them (ev:ev-mv3u16vc-014dd303).
findings.recommendation: Owner: the ECCode toolkit (file as a TK item; dispatch learning-debugger only if the cause is disputed). Resolved when treeDigest hashes dirty files by paths git resolves correctly, with a regression test: in a project below the repository root, one modified tracked file and one untracked file give a non-null digest that changes with either file.

findings.detail: The security reviewer ran the race 25 times, with the same result each time. The new FK refuses reserve's insert, and toAppError maps it to 500. findings.title: (security) the read fail-open allows uncounted reads only while another connection holds the lock; a user cannot cause it
findings.detail: From the security draft. 40 concurrent writes plus 120 reads by one user were all counted, with no busy_open line, because the app uses a single synchronous connection. While the lock was held, reads throttled the process to about 18 per second. Accepted by design.
findings.recommendation: No action. Resolved by this record.

findings.title: (security, outside this diff) the session touch on a GET still waits the full busy timeout synchronously
findings.detail: From the security draft. A GET took 1057 ms under a held lock with a 1000 ms busy timeout (src/auth/sessions.js, the touch UPDATE). This is the same class as TR-R4-3.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the next src/auth touch. Resolved when the touch uses the short wait or skips on busy, with a lock-holder test; or the orchestrator records it as accepted.

findings.title: (security) collisions made before 006 stay as they are
findings.detail: Confirmed on a 005 database filled through the app: a model_spend row naming a reused id is unchanged after 006. This cannot be repaired from the data, and the submission discloses it.
findings.recommendation: No action. Resolved by this record.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
Condition met.
- take() fails open only for GET and HEAD and only on a busy error, uncounted, with one rate_limit.busy_open line that carries the request id only.
- Reads wait at most 50 ms, and the timeout is restored.
- State-changing methods, and a call with no method, fail closed with 503 DB_BUSY.
- The hook passes req.method, which cannot be spoofed: there is no override header or parameter, as the security reviewer confirmed.
- Through createApp, a signed-in GET answers 200 under a held lock and a POST answers 503 (P1).
- The pre-rework limiter fails the lock-holder tests, and all limiter and hook mutants are killed.
The change to 006 that SEC-RW4-1 requires does not touch these files.

When another process holds or awaits a write lock while this connection holds a shared one, waiting could deadlock, so SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and never calls the busy handler, so busy_timeout does not help. Reproduced with the reviewer's script (ev:ev-mv1hf138-016b38f3: 3 of 40 sequential runs failed with 'database is locked'; the script always exits 0, so the counts are the result) and with a minimal probe (.eccode/drafts/b1-pb1-probe.mjs, error code 5 from the WAL switch, about 1 in 180 opens). Fix in src/db/connection.js: openDb reads the journal mode first and switches only when the file is not WAL, and both that step and the later pragmas run under retryWhileBusy, a bounded back-off (2 ms doubling to 50 ms with jitter) on SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED up to max(busyTimeoutMs, 1000 ms), after which the busy error is rethrown; the handle is closed on failure. New test/unit/db/open-race.test.js (all named PB-1): retry unit tests, bounded give-up against a real lock-holder process, success when the holder releases, and a stress of 25 rounds x 4 processes on a fresh file. ho-mv1jewhq-01c5bca8.completedWork: Algorithm (new src/domain/search.js, used by planner.js): the search enumerates offer SUBSETS within the pickup cap, smallest first, and solves each subset's covering problem exactly by bounded depth-first search. Pickups, plan-ready time and the supplier-code string depend on the subset alone, so inside a subset only total and vector matter. Pruning is valid and exact: (1) only irredundant plans are enumerated (the optimum is always irredundant: dropping a bundle never raises total, pickups or ready time and gives a smaller vector; the forced offer of a cheapest-cover query is exempt); (2) multiplicities are looped only inside the window [kLo, kHi] that the remaining demand allows; (3) a fractional-knapsack lower bound per dimension (mandatory later bundles, prep fees of unused suppliers, tax-rate scaling less one cent of rounding per touched order) cuts subtrees above the budget or the K-th best plan; (4) ascending canonical vector order lets a subtree that can only tie the K-th best of the same subset be cut, which removes equal-cost plateaus; (5) when no supplier has two members, a dominance table keyed by (position, cups, lids) keeps the K cheapest prefixes per state. Subsets are pre-filtered by a cheap root bound (cover floor plus prep sums). For infeasible requests the cheapest unconstrained cover answers every offer it uses, and any other offer is searched with that cover plus one bundle as its starting incumbent. Results: reproduction (stock 100, 10,000 cups, budget USD 100,000, maxPickups 5) now returns A at 301,000 cents in 0.1 ms, same as maxPickups 1. Sweep: 5,400 inputs, no PLANNER_LIMIT, worst single call 21.5 ms (was 237-305 ms with refusals). Stress (draft b2-planner-stress.mjs): 8,000 seeded-shape inputs with availability up to 100,000, quantities up to 100,000, differing cup/lid quantities and tax: worst 9.7 ms, no limit; 3,000 random-priced 12-offer catalogs: worst 36 ms; 3,000 catalogs with several offers per supplier: worst 23 ms. Tests added: planner-oracle.property.test.js gains (a) brute-force oracle on larger stock (availability up to 7, 100 catalogs), (b) tie-heavy catalogs against the oracle (equal prices, prep fees, ready times, several offers per supplier, 120 catalogs), (c) identical tied offers of one supplier, (d) 250 medium catalogs (availability up to 12, up to 6 offers, quantities up to 3000) against the frozen slow exact reference test/unit/domain/helpers/reference-planner.js, comparing the whole output; planner-fixture.test.js replaces the old absurd-input test with 'SEC-B-1: huge stock and quantity are solved exactly' (12 offers of single cups, 100,000 each, solved in well under 1 s) and a guard test of the node cap through search(..., {maxNodes}); test/timing/planner-sec-b1.test.js has the named test, a 1,008-call grid over the seeded shape (stock 1..100,000, quantity 100..100,000, no PLANNER_LIMIT, each < 100 ms, p95 < 20 ms) and 150 random 12-offer catalogs (each < 250 ms). A mutation (pruning ties across different subsets) was caught by the reference comparison and reverted. The earlier suites (RS-06..RS-11, 500-catalog oracle property, derive totality, states, money, time, explain, NFR5) pass unchanged.
remainingIssues: PLANNER_LIMIT (2,000,000 nodes per search, about 150 ms) is still a real guard, not an unreachable one. It is not reached by the seeded catalog shape, by random-priced catalogs of up to 12 offers, or by catalogs with several offers per supplier within the API ranges (evidence above). It CAN still be reached, and calls can take 150-400 ms (up to about 800 ms when several searches hit it), by deliberately tie-laden catalogs: several suppliers whose bundles of different size cost the same per bundle, quantity of about 50,000 or more, and especially a non-zero tax rate (rounding noise defeats tie pruning); and by catalogs whose bundles hold different numbers of cups and lids (not reachable through the API, which only seeds equal counts) at quantity 100,000. Measured with the adversarial draft script b2-planner-stress.mjs: about 0.1-0.3 % of such inputs hit the cap (ev:ev-mv1jdvnv-01ed0f76 is that script's recorded run and shows one 58 ms call; it exits 1 by design because the script treats any call over 50 ms as a failure). A supplier can set equal prices through PATCH, so this is reachable in principle; exactness for those needs an integer DP over coverage that I did not build in this round. Recommended in c2 regardless: map PlannerLimitError (RangeError, code PLANNER_LIMIT) to a typed 422/503, and add the per-customer rate limit on POST /api/requests/:id/plan and on re-plan drains that the security draft asks for (item 3 of its resolution).

ho-mv2pgzqg-0145c52b.completedWork: ROUTES (src/routes/auth.js): GET csrf, POST register, POST signin (public; they run Origin + pre-login-or-session CSRF themselves), POST signout (policy session), GET session (public, uses ctx.auth.identify). Cookie rs_sid=<43 chars>; Path=/; Max-Age=43200; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (+Secure when RS_PUBLIC_URL is https); sign-out sends Max-Age=0. Sessions (src/auth/sessions.js): 32 random bytes, only sha256 stored, idle 60 min (last_seen refreshed at most once a minute, a busy DB on that refresh is ignored), absolute 12 h, disabled users do not resolve, disableUser deletes sessions. Sign-in and register destroy the incoming session in the same transaction that creates the new one (SEC-20); an attacker-planted id is never adopted. CSRF (src/auth/csrf.js): pre-login token nonce.hmac (nonce = 8-byte time + 16 random bytes, HMAC-SHA256 with meta csrf_key, 2 h, small future skew), session token compared in constant time, Origin must equal RS_PUBLIC_URL's origin or http(s)://<Host>. Throttle (src/auth/throttle.js): an attempt is counted when admitted, in the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE as the check (so parallel requests cannot overshoot); pair >=5 -> 429 signin_pair, IP >=20 -> 429 signin_ip, both before the password check; >=10 failures for the username across IPs -> delay min(10,(n-9)) s then the password is still checked; success deletes that pair's rows including its own reservation; unknown usernames take the same path and one scrypt against a dummy hash with the seed's parameters; 401 body is identical for unknown, wrong password and disabled. Register limit uses rate_events kind register, key ip:<addr>, reserved after validation and before hashing. Password (src/auth/password.js): async scrypt N=16384 r=8 p=1 key 64, accepts only that format, never throws on malformed hashes. Client IP (src/auth/client-ip.js, FU-11): socket address by default; X-Forwarded-For is ignored unless RS_TRUST_PROXY=1, then only the last hop and only if net.isIP accepts it (IPv4-mapped IPv6 collapsed, IPv6 lower-cased), else the socket address; an invalid value never becomes a throttle key. RBAC (src/auth/rbac.js): authorize(ctx, route) for non-public routes: policy signature is allowed only for POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey (no session, no CSRF) else 403; Origin check on non-GET first; no session -> 401; role mismatch -> 403 FORBIDDEN; then X-CSRF-Token must equal the session token (403 CSRF_FAILED). Admin (src/services/users.js ensureAdmin, called from main.js): scrypt hash from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD, disabled row with an unusable hash when unset, password change or disable ends the admin sessions, a non-admin 'admin' row stops startup. Audit (src/services/audit.js): sanitised detail (ids and codes only) for auth.signin ok/failed/denied, auth.signout, auth.register ok/failed/denied. src/app.js: builds deps.auth, default access hook is the RBAC hook, an injected authorize still replaces it (b1's test double contract unchanged), ctx gains session/sessionId/identified, clientIp moved to src/auth/client-ip.js. TESTS: test/api/auth.test.js (52 cases) and test/unit/auth/* (67 cases). Criteria to evidence: all of them by ev:ev-mv2pf62t-01198c9f (119 tests pass under the net guard; the test names start with ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-9, SEC-13, SEC-20, SEC-B-9, F-TR-17, RS-30, FU-6, T6); failing state before any work ev:ev-mv2p31zi-01021921; full suite npm test 509/509 and NFR5 p95 92 ms ev:ev-mv2pg2ag-0141772a. Decisions: (1) X-Forwarded-For is not trusted by default (spec default is no proxy). (2) The access hook is only called for non-public routes (b1 contract, and b1's own tests register public POST routes), so the two public POST routes check CSRF inside their handlers. (3) Rejecting validation failures before the throttle: a 422 uses no register budget and no sign-in failure row.
remainingIssues: AUTHORIZE HOOK CONTRACT for c2/c3/e-tasks: do not pass an authorize to createApp. Declare the policy on router.add: 'customer' | 'supplier' | 'admin' | 'session' (any signed-in role). The hook runs before the handler and sets ctx.user = {id, username, displayName, role, supplierId, supplierCode}, ctx.session = {idHash, csrfToken, createdAt, expiresAt}, ctx.sessionId. Anonymous 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, wrong role 403 FORBIDDEN, bad Origin or missing/wrong X-CSRF-Token on any non-GET 403 CSRF_FAILED. Scope queries by ctx.user.id (customer) or ctx.user.supplierId (supplier) in SQL. toPublicUser(user) in src/services/users.js gives the contract User object.

Public routes that need the user (PayPal return/cancel 'anonymous -> 303 to sign-in' in the RBAC matrix, per e2) must be registered with policy 'public' and call ctx.auth.identify(ctx) (returns the user or null, never throws) or ctx.auth.requireRole(ctx, ...roles) (401/403). A policy 'customer' route cannot redirect an anonymous caller. A public state-changing route gets no automatic CSRF check: it must call checkOrigin and a token check itself (see guardPreLogin in src/routes/auth.js). test/unit/auth/rbac.test.js asserts that the only public non-GET routes are POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/signin, so a task that adds another will see that test fail and must decide deliberately (update the list in that test, which is owned by c1 and would need a rework or a one-line change agreed with the orchestrator).

The webhook route (e3) must be registered as POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey with policy 'signature'; the hook skips session and CSRF for exactly that method and template and returns 403 for any other 'signature' route. Its own per-IP rate limit (60/min, 'webhook_ip') and ctx.clientIp() are the task's job.

ensureAdmin({db, config, clock}) runs in src/main.js startApp only. Tests that use test/helpers/app-harness.js do not get an admin account unless they call ensureAdmin themselves (see test/api/auth.test.js), and createApp does not provision it. The harness also does not run main.js, so no csrf_key row exists beforehand: createAuth creates it lazily with getOrCreateMeta.

The general per-user limit (300 requests/min, details.limit 'general') and the webhook/extract limits are not part of c1 and are not implemented here; rate_events kind 'general' exists in the schema. If no later task owns the general limit, the delivery lead should assign it (it would sit in the access hook after identification).

The cross-IP delay (1-10 s) uses a real timer (auth.sleep, injectable through createAuth), so API tests that exercise it take about 1 s each and pass record:false to keep NFR5 samples clean. Fixed-clock tests do not make it faster.

IPv6 clients can rotate through a /64 to get a fresh per-IP budget: the throttle key is the full address (the spec says per IP). Not changed; a /64 key would be a small change in src/auth/client-ip.js if the security reviewer wants it.
Registration reveals USERNAME_TAKEN (accepted in the spec as T24 note) and counts against the register budget, which is what limits enumeration.
Latency samples: the sign-in/register tests record their requests through the harness as usual (scrypt is about 50 ms); p95 over the whole suite was 92 ms in the full run.
The seeded RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD check is config's (>= 16 chars, placeholder refusal); ensureAdmin trusts config. The raw environment value is only held in the Secret and in the scrypt call.

Migration 006 is app-only. The runner (src/db/migrate.js) applies a file inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE with foreign_keys = ON, which cannot be switched off inside a transaction, so the rebuild uses defer_foreign_keys = ON and TEMP staging tables. DROP TABLE runs an implicit DELETE that fires ON DELETE CASCADE, so extractions, requirements, replan_queue and plan_approvals are staged and put back with their ids; non-cascading children (reservations, supplier_orders, payment_operations, provider_calls) stay and are satisfied again when the parent ids are re-inserted; a parent that does not come back fails the COMMIT on the deferred foreign key and rolls everything back. Tables are recreated under their own names, so no RENAME rewrites other tables. The SEC-B-2 triggers sit on audit_events and inventory_ledger, which are not touched. CHOICE for model_spend.request_id: FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES rescue_requests(id) ON DELETE SET NULL. The row is the budget ledger (gate.js sums every row of the day), so it must survive a hard delete of its request, and SET NULL drops only the pointer so it can never name another request; an insert naming a request that does not exist is refused. A CHECK cannot look at another table, and a tombstone reference would add a second source of truth to keep. Rows that already point at a deleted request are copied with NULL. The 'after 5 failed drains the next step is REPLAN' rule is derive.js's and already works from failed_drains.

Stale model-spend rows (FU-22 owner): both the retention sweep (d3) and reconciler housekeeping call gate.settleStale; it is one compare-and-set UPDATE on status = 'reserved', so a row settles once whichever runs first. d3's call was left in place (not my file).

Stock helpers: consume and restock ledger rows are written by local functions in saga.js because services/ledger.js (c3) has no consume/restock function. They follow ledger.js's row format and the SUM(delta) invariant is asserted in the tests; moving them into ledger.js is a later tidy-up.

The webhook route (e3) moves operations without running the compensation hook for captured; the reconciler backstop (step 6) queues the refund on its next tick instead. If e3's file is touched later it should call queueRefundWhenCancelled (exported from saga.js) in the same transaction.

RESERVATION_EXPIRED on execute also runs the expiry pass inline (expireDueReservations) so the answer and the stored state agree: the plan becomes non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED), stock released, voids sent. The spec does not say; it is the same pass the reconciler would run.

A authorization expired/voided found when a void is refused (resolveRejectedVoid, e2) ends as void_failed by the spec's 'anything else' rule; step 2 compensation after an authorization the provider already shows VOIDED ends voided (the void is refused, getAuthorization says VOIDED).

Not covered here by design: the two-OS-process execute test (e6), SIGKILL/SIGSTOP restart and lease-takeover tests with real processes (f4); the in-process fence test uses a second saga identity over the same database, and the freeze hooks were not used. LIVE-DEPENDENT: real PayPal behaviour of final_capture, DUPLICATE_INVOICE_ID on the capture invoice id (rs-so-<id>-cap), AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED semantics and request-id retention is unverified until test:live-paypal runs (OQ-D5).
Mutation proofs have no ev ids (plain runs in a scratch copy of the project); the list is in completedWork.

NOTES FOR e6/f1/f4: execute answers 202 {claimed:true, plan:{id,status:'executing'}, requestId} or 200 {claimed:false, plan:{id,status}, rescueStatus, requestId}; refusals are 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED, PLAN_NOT_EXECUTABLE (details.reason), RESERVATION_EXPIRED, AUTHORIZATION_PENDING, AUTHORIZATION_MISSING, COMMITMENT_MISSING, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, INVALID_STATE (plan not approved, or approved without any reservation), each audited as denied. Fault names used: lost_response:<kind> (effect applied), timeout:<kind> (nothing applied), http_429/422/500:<kind>, capture_declined, capture_pending, refund_pending, refund_failed, authorize_pending, authorize_denied, crash_after_return_commit, capture_lands_after_void_intent. For f4 (restart recovery): a stale started intent becomes unknown after 2 x RS_PAYPAL_TIMEOUT_MS (error_code STALE_INTENT); takeover needs lease_until <= now and happens only when no operation is capture_pending/unknown; the resumed saga repeats step 2 when every capture has send_count 0, else resumes at step 3 and re-sends an unknown capture (same key) only after the reconciler restored the operation to authorized by reading. For f1: supersession of an approved plan still goes through ctx.voidRule; the execute claim refuses a superseded plan and a plan whose authorization expiry is inside the margin runs markNonExecutable(AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED) in the refusal's transaction.

dec-mv33a9jm-0122049d.rationale: The rework deletes a filter inside one browser test and changes no runtime code, route, policy or hook. Raised as TR-RW3-2 (info). Rework-3's change is held by commit 7942bf2 (TR-RW3-3).

dec-mv341ap0-010209d2.title: FU-23 rework needs the user's authorization
dec-mv341ap0-010209d2.decision: The engine refused rework-4 (USER_AUTH_REQUIRED: limits.maxReworks=3 reached). Only b1 (phase B, approved) owns src/db/**, so the AUTOINCREMENT migration cannot ride any pending task. The orchestrator asks the user either to open the rework as the user actor or to grant a rework.open delegation for rework-4. Until then phase E proceeds through e0..e3; e4 is not dispatched (TR-D-3's condition), and FU-23 stays open as minor.
dec-mv341ap0-010209d2.rationale: Reworks past the limit are the user's call by design: three reworks after review point at the plan (here: b1 planned every migration and no later task owns the directory). Blocking phase E entirely would waste the budget on a minor finding the reviewers did not block on.

dec-mv34dqsr-0163a6d9.title: Live-runner ceiling refuses a leading zero
dec-mv34dqsr-0163a6d9.decision: The ceiling must be written as 0, or a non-zero whole part without a leading zero, with at most two decimals (0.01 to 5.00). 05 and 005.00 are refused.
dec-mv34dqsr-0163a6d9.rationale: One exact form per value keeps the check unambiguous; the refusal message states the rule. ai-engineer asked (d2 reset handoff ho-mv34d3dh-01f6abfa). Reversible by widening the pattern.

dec-mv35aank-0169ec16.title: SEC-D-12: image provenance only for product fields
dec-mv35aank-0169ec16.decision: Provenance image is accepted only for productType, material, capacityMl and diameterMm. A model answer that claims image provenance for cupQuantity, lidQuantity, maxPickups, deadline or budget is downgraded to unknown with the field's question, whatever the photo shows.
dec-mv35aank-0169ec16.rationale: Security iteration 2 (phase-d-security-2.md) showed that once a photo is attached a model can bypass the text grounding (TR-D-1, SEC-D-10, SEC-D-11) for every field by claiming image provenance; the server cannot read the photo's wording. Photos show the product; quantities, pickups, deadline and budget come from the buyer's text or are entered by hand. Reversible; owner d3 (src/services/extraction.js) or a later rework if phase D is approved first.

dec-mv36cgqs-01f68eb5.title: FU-32: the adapter charges the cap for any started call it kills
dec-mv36cgqs-01f68eb5.decision: Accepted: a CLI call killed by the adapter's own timeout, an abort or the output flood after a child has started is charged at the per-call cap, like a call killed by close() or by the service watchdog.
dec-mv36cgqs-01f68eb5.rationale: Once a child has started, the real spend is unknown and bounded only by the cap; charging the cap keeps the ledger conservative and consistent across all kill paths (TR-D-15's principle). Reversible by ai-engineer under FU-26.

dec-mv36cgyj-01f0741d.title: FU-30 and FU-31: deadline date part and Arabic am/pm are accepted residuals
dec-mv36cgyj-01f0741d.decision: For version one, a user_text deadline is grounded on its time only (the date part is not checked), and Arabic am/pm markers are not read (such deadlines become unknown and are asked). Both stay listed as residuals in the verification report; they ride FU-23's rework-4 if the user authorizes it, owner backend-engineer.
dec-mv36cgyj-01f0741d.rationale: The buyer confirms every deadline before planning and approves the plan before any payment; an unread marker fails in the safe direction. No task after d3 owns the extraction service and the rework limit is reached (dec-mv341ap0-010209d2).

dec-mv36ch5t-01a1d509.title: SEC-D-13: grounding stays lexical
dec-mv36ch5t-01a1d509.decision: The unit-or-currency-token requirement for capacity, diameter and budget quotes is not adopted in version one. Grounding is lexical (presence, whole-number alignment, field-specific rules for the deadline and image provenance).
dec-mv36ch5t-01a1d509.rationale: The remaining cases (a quote that belongs to another field, codes, idioms) show the mismatch in the quote displayed next to the value, the buyer confirms the fields, and the plan is approved before payment. Reversible; owner backend-engineer with ai-engineer if adopted later.

dec-mv38g19z-01f0a99f.title: FU-25 amended: the rephrase variable stays parsed, documented as having no effect
dec-mv38g19z-01f0a99f.decision: src/config.js keeps parsing RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE (default 0) exactly as before; the opt-in rephrasing stays unwired; g2 documents in README and .env.example that the variable is reserved and has no effect in version one. This replaces the removal ordered by dec-mv330t7a-017a2211.
dec-mv38g19z-01f0a99f.rationale: The removal in e1 broke four tests in test/unit/config/defaults.test.js, test/unit/config/limits.test.js and test/scan/env-example.test.js, owned only by the approved phase B tasks b1 and b4; no later task owns them and the rework limit is reached (dec-mv341ap0-010209d2). A green suite before the phase E submission outweighs removing one parsed-but-unused variable. Reversible under a user-authorized rework.

dec-mv39rg82-01a682bc.title: SEC-R-1 joins the user-authorized rework-4 scope
dec-mv39rg82-01a682bc.decision: SEC-R-1 (src/auth/general-limit.js takes the write lock on every signed-in GET; fix: fail open on a busy error for GET and HEAD only, with a lock-holder test) cannot ride any pending task: only c1 (approved) owns src/auth/**. It is added to the scope the orchestrator asks the user to authorize as rework-4, together with FU-23. e4 is not dispatched before both land.
dec-mv39rg82-01a682bc.rationale: The phase D reviews required SEC-R-1 before e4; the rework limit is reached (dec-mv341ap0-010209d2).

dec-mv3abkne-01161cf3.title: Webhooks: an unmapped event type is invalid (400), not ignored
dec-mv3abkne-01161cf3.decision: The webhook route keeps e3's behaviour: an event whose event_type is not one of the seven mapped types fails the pre-checks and is stored as an invalid row with EVENT_TYPE_NOT_MAPPED and answered 400, before any provider call. The runbook (g2) must say to subscribe the PayPal webhook only to the seven mapped event types.
dec-mv3abkne-01161cf3.rationale: The spec's event list says unknown types are ignored while its pre-check requires a mapped type; the task's acceptance criterion chose the pre-check, which keeps SEC-6's rule that junk never reaches the provider. Reversible: one line in precheck() and one test table.

dec-mv3abkv0-011839e9.title: RS_PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ALGOS stays an environment fallback until phase G
dec-mv3abkv0-011839e9.decision: webhookAlgos() reads config.paypalWebhookAlgos when present, else the RS_PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ALGOS environment variable, else SHA256withRSA. g2 lists the variable in .env.example and the README; the config field is added only if the env-example scan can stay green with it (g2 reports).
dec-mv3abkv0-011839e9.rationale: src/config.js (e1) and .env.example (g2) are owned by tasks in different phases and the env-example scan ties them together; adding one side alone turns the suite red. Reversible.

dec-mv3sg8cv-0146d001.title: The user raised maxReworks to 4 and maxRuntimeMinutes to 2400
dec-mv3sg8cv-0146d001.decision: Commits d5e3695 and 1efcab5 (author TOUMO45, GitHub web editor) raise limits.maxRuntimeMinutes to 2400 and limits.maxReworks to 4. The orchestrator opens rework-4 (FU-23 and SEC-R-1) under that authorization and resumes phase E.
dec-mv3sg8cv-0146d001.rationale: Both limits are reserved for the user; the user chose the config edit over the CLI command. Recorded so the authorization trail is explicit.

dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152.title: FU-33: the uploads-retention timer test race is mitigated, not removed
dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152.decision: e4's startApp now starts the reconciler's first tick only after the startup retention pass resolves, which removes the load that exposed the race; the test itself (d3's file, phase D approved) still checks the image file immediately after the row disappears. The one-line test fix (wait for the file as well as the row) is carried to phase G as FU-33 and to the verification report; if the test fails again before then, it is re-run once and reported, never skipped.
dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152.rationale: No remaining task owns test/api/uploads-retention.test.js and the rework limit is used; the product behaviour (row deleted, then file unlinked, both within the sweep) is correct.

dec-mv3u4zr4-0165c54d.title: e4 was dispatched in parallel with rework-4
dec-mv3u4zr4-0165c54d.decision: The orchestrator dispatched e4 at the same time as rework-4 instead of after it, contrary to dec-mv39rg82-01a682bc and TR-D-3's ordering. phase:e-payments is submitted for review only after phase:rework-4 is approved, and the phase E reviewers re-run the suite with both landed.
dec-mv3u4zr4-0165c54d.rationale: e4 owns none of rework-4's nine files; the technical reviewer (TR-R4-8) confirmed the risk is contained with a green full run on e4's final code. Recorded so the deviation is explicit.

dec-mv3u4zzu-01f07c5a.title: Migration 006 run time is documented, not optimized
dec-mv3u4zzu-01f07c5a.decision: Migration 006 holds the write lock while it copies; its run time grows roughly quadratically (about 9 s at 5,000 request trees, TR-R4-1). The README and the verification report (g2) state: upgrade with a single process before traffic. The migration is not changed.
dec-mv3u4zzu-01f07c5a.rationale: Demo and pilot databases hold far fewer rows; once approved the migration checksum is frozen, and temporary indexes would add risk to a reviewed migration for no benefit at this scale.
